1	Fine-grained structured pruning of reasoning Large Language Models (LLMs), which removes multi-layer perceptron (MLP) channel groups rather than entire layers, is typically followed by Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) or Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) to restore reasoning capabilities.
2	RLVR is widely believed to be superior, yet we show this hierarchy reflects suboptimal pruning, not a fundamental property of RL\@.
3	When pruning preserves representational diversity, recovery method choice becomes irrelevant, a phenomenon we term \emph{reward-accuracy decoupling}: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and SFT produce near-identical accuracy despite vastly different reward trajectories, a pattern that holds at moderate sparsity (20--25\%) across benchmarks.
4	We propose Recovery-Aware Structured Pruning (\rasp{}), which balances gradient importance with Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA)-based representational diversity via a coefficient $\alpha$.
5	On DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B at 20\% sparsity, a dose-response analysis reveals an inverted-U in recovery accuracy, peaking at $\alpha{=}2.0$ (66.11\% on GSM8K).
6	Under GRPO training, four pruning criteria produce a \emph{recovery capacity spectrum}: diversity-preserving pruning achieves active learning (peak reward 4.4$\times$ vs importance-only), while importance-dominated pruning collapses entirely.
7	The spectrum tracks preserved representational diversity rather than gradient importance, with preliminary evidence at 1.5B scale and, via SFT-based recovery, across Qwen2.5-family models (Qwen2.5-Math-7B).

1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
2	\label{sec:conclusion}
3	
4	Whether RLVR outperforms SFT for recovering pruned reasoning models depends on how the model was pruned.
5	Under diversity-preserving pruning at 20--25\% sparsity, the two paradigms produce near-identical accuracy (mean $|\Delta| {=} 0.54$\,pp; max $1.8$\,pp), yet the pruning criterion creates a 4.4$\times$ peak reward gap.
6	SFT warmup performs the bulk of accuracy recovery (${\sim}$60\,pp); GRPO exposes structural capacity differences but adds negligible accuracy, a pattern confirmed at 300 steps where CKA-only reward rises yet accuracy remains unchanged.
7	CKA-only preserves distinct pathways that sustain RL exploration (\S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}); the non-monotonic $\alpha$ dose-response argues against a layer-distribution confound.

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

Whether RLVR outperforms SFT for recovering pruned reasoning models depends on how the model was pruned.
Under diversity-preserving pruning at 20--25\% sparsity, the two paradigms produce near-identical accuracy (mean $|\Delta| {=} 0.54$\,pp; max $1.8$\,pp), yet the pruning criterion creates a 4.4$\times$ peak reward gap.
SFT warmup performs the bulk of accuracy recovery (${\sim}$60\,pp); GRPO exposes structural capacity differences but adds negligible accuracy, a pattern confirmed at 300 steps where CKA-only reward rises yet accuracy remains unchanged.
CKA-only preserves distinct pathways that sustain RL exploration (\S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}); the non-monotonic $\alpha$ dose-response argues against a layer-distribution confound.

\paragraph{Diagnostic role of GRPO.}
The reward-accuracy decoupling suggests that, at moderate sparsity, GRPO functions as a \emph{diagnostic probe} for pruning quality rather than a recovery enhancer.
Reward trajectories reveal whether the pruned architecture retains sufficient diversity for RL exploration---information invisible to SFT, which converges to similar accuracy regardless of the underlying structural capacity.
This diagnostic perspective reframes the practical question from ``which recovery method is better?'' to ``does the pruned model still support RL exploration?''

\paragraph{Sparsity-dependent decoupling.}
The decoupling is not absolute: at 15\% sparsity, GRPO amplifies the CKA-guided advantage ($+$1.51\,pp differential), while at 20--25\% the paradigms converge.
This suggests a transition: at lower sparsity, sufficient capacity headroom remains for GRPO to differentiate methods; at moderate sparsity, SFT already captures most recoverable capacity.
The boundary and its relationship to model capacity warrant future investigation.

\paragraph{Practitioner implications.}
For deployment pipelines that include post-pruning RL training, diversity-preserving criteria (CKA-only or high-$\alpha$ \rasp{}) should be preferred, as they maintain the exploration pathways that RL requires.
Our findings complement \citet{selfhealing2025}: while they demonstrate RLVR superiority for unstructured magnitude pruning at 96.5\% retention, we show this hierarchy dissolves under diversity-preserving structured pruning at 80\% retention---the gap is an artifact of the pruning criterion, not a fundamental property of RL recovery.

Code and evaluation scripts are available at \url{https://github.com/anonymous-nlp-2026/recovery_aware_struct_prune}.

\paragraph{Recovery pipeline and hardware.}
All four methods undergo matched two-stage recovery.
Stage~1 (SFT warmup): 2 epochs on 7{,}473 GSM8K chain-of-thought examples with teacher forcing (37 minutes), restoring EOS generation and basic format compliance.

All methods use identical GRPO configuration with \texttt{max\_completion\_length}{$=$}1{,}024, except Random which uses the TRL default of 512 tokens (Table~\ref{tab:hyperparams}; Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_training}), making it a conservative comparison point.

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

Whether RLVR outperforms SFT for recovering pruned reasoning models depends on how the model was pruned.
Under diversity-preserving pruning at 20--25\% sparsity, the two paradigms produce near-identical accuracy (mean $|\Delta| {=} 0.54$\,pp; max $1.8$\,pp), yet the pruning criterion creates a 4.4$\times$ peak reward gap.
SFT warmup performs the bulk of accuracy recovery (${\sim}$60\,pp); GRPO exposes structural capacity differences but adds negligible accuracy, a pattern confirmed at 300 steps where CKA-only reward rises yet accuracy remains unchanged (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_extended}).
CKA-only preserves distinct pathways that sustain RL exploration (\S\ref{sec:extended_analysis}); the non-monotonic $\alpha$ dose-response argues against a layer-distribution confound.

\paragraph{GRPO as diagnostic probe.}
The decoupling suggests that GRPO functions as a \emph{diagnostic probe} for pruning quality rather than a recovery enhancer at moderate sparsity: reward trajectories reveal whether the pruned architecture retains sufficient diversity for RL exploration---information invisible to SFT, which converges to similar accuracy regardless.
This reframes the practical question from ``which recovery method?'' to ``does the pruned model support RL exploration?''
The decoupling is not absolute: at 15\% sparsity, GRPO amplifies the CKA-guided advantage ($+$1.51\,pp differential), suggesting that at lower sparsity sufficient headroom remains for GRPO to differentiate; the transition boundary warrants future investigation.

\paragraph{Implications.}
For deployment pipelines that include post-pruning RL, diversity-preserving criteria (CKA-only or high-$\alpha$ \rasp{}) should be preferred, as they maintain the exploration pathways that RL requires.
Our findings complement \citet{selfhealing2025}: while they demonstrate RLVR superiority for unstructured magnitude pruning at 96.5\% retention, we show this hierarchy dissolves under diversity-preserving structured pruning at 80\% retention---the gap is an artifact of the pruning criterion, not a fundamental property of RL recovery.

Code and evaluation scripts are available at \url{https://github.com/anonymous-nlp-2026/recovery_aware_struct_prune}.
